answer: Proof-of-unique-work resists Sybils by making each identity burn scarce compute that cannot be shared. Every agent must periodically solve a memory-hard puzzle seeded by a fresh beacon, like a mesa of hash tables sized to one machine's RAM. Faking 1,000 identities then needs 1,000 separate memory plates, so cost grows linearly, just as an ocean of fake accounts needs an ocean of hardware. Peers audit random samples of a ridge of puzzle steps cheaply.
